units.title: Established alternative L1s
angles: Faces. Find every way one balance at the PoolManager can be reached under two currency ids or in two units on this network (native asset with an ERC-20 face, wrapped native predeploys, bridged and canonical versions sharing storage, tokens with more than one entry point), and walk sync, settle, take, mint and burn across the two faces in every order.

Pooled assets. Read the PoolManager's largest token balances on this network from chain. For each token, check transfer and balanceOf for behaviour any holder can trigger: rebasing, fees, callbacks, share accounting, special recipients, special amounts.

units.title: Arbitrum Nitro and Orbit chains
angles: Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

Sweep. List every precompile, predeploy, system contract, face of the native asset, wrapped native token, bridge, staking and fee contract on this network. For each one, run eth_call with "from" set to the PoolManager address for the call shapes P1, P2, P3 and P5 in ASSUMPTIONS.md (empty calldata with zero value, transfer(address,uint256) with zero and nonzero amount, balanceOf(PoolManager), and each IHooks selector), and record what comes back. Follow up on every target that does not revert.

units.title: OP Stack chains with ETH gas
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Known weaknesses. Collect security advisories, audit reports, bug bounty write-ups, incident post-mortems and open issues for this network's execution client, precompiles and system contracts from the last two years, including behaviour the network calls by design. For each, decide whether an ordinary account could use it against funds in the PoolManager.

code.task: The repository's own tests, NatSpec comments and test doubles are the only permitted reference for what the source is meant to do. Replay by reading or by Python transcription every concrete expectation in test/PoolManager.t.sol, test/PoolManager.swap.t.sol, test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol, test/PoolManagerInitialize.t.sol, test/ModifyLiquidity.t.sol, test/Sync.t.sol, test/CustomAccounting.t.sol, test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol, test/NoDelegateCall.t.sol, test/DynamicFees.t.sol, test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol, test/SkipCallsTestHook.t.sol, test/Extsload.t.sol, test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.t.sol and test/types/Currency.t.sol against the source in src/, including every expectRevert selector and every asserted number. Compare each NatSpec comment in src/interfaces/ with what the implementation does. Read the helper contracts in src/test/ and test/utils/ for behaviour the production code is expected to have. Every place where the source cannot produce what a test or comment states is a candidate: decide whether it gives an ordinary account a way to take or lock funds.

The repository's own tests are the only permitted reference for what the libraries are meant to compute. Replay by Python transcription every concrete vector and boundary in test/libraries/ (TickMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, FullMath, BitMath, UnsafeMath, TickBitmap, Position, SafeCast, LiquidityMath, LPFeeLibrary, ProtocolFeeLibrary, Hooks, Lock, StateLibrary, Pool, and the rest), test/Tick.t.sol and test/types/, against the source in src/libraries/ and src/types/. Use the gas snapshot files in snapshots/ as a second witness: a snapshot that the source could not plausibly produce marks a changed code path. Every vector, revert or boundary the source cannot reproduce is a candidate: decide whether it gives an ordinary account a way to take or lock funds.
